_comment: Register pointers whose cited LINE CONTENT differs from the revision that wrote them, each with a written `reason` saying which PR re-pins it or why nothing does. The screen FAILS on any drift not listed here and reports entries that no longer drift as STALE (non-failing, prune them). `regLines` are the register sentences the cite silences — the screen matches on cite, so one entry can cover several. Regenerate preserving reasons: node scripts/check-register-drift.mjs --update

entries.reason: Read-log, not a pointer: PP-055 lists the auto-backup line set (55, 147, 243, 256-257, 297) as ranges somebody read, and #2441 declined to re-pin it for exactly that reason — re-pinning would invent an intent the entry never stated. Listed here so the decision is on the record instead of silent drift.

History, not a live pointer: the register line this names is PP-068's bullet, which reports the coordinate as it found it — `docs/README.md:71` was where the README paragraph sat then, and it now sits at `docs/README.md:75`. Re-writing PP-068's sentence would falsify the measurement it records. #2534 (PP-070) and #2507 (PP-065) are open with their own re-pins of the live cite, so whichever docs PR merges last re-derives this entry; prune it the day the README names the rule by heading text instead of a line number.

Chronic, not accidental: every register entry adds header text, and the sentence these lines quote is the README's own re-pin of the pointer INTO the register — so any new entry moves the line the pointer names and this cite reads as drift by construction. PP-072 (#2556, merged) minted it with the rule at :4651; PP-073 (#2528) re-pinned it to :4774; PP-074 (#2526) re-pins it to :4903, the eleventh time. #2534 (PP-070) and #2507 (PP-065) are still open re-pinning the same sentence from their own trees, so whichever docs PR merges last re-derives this entry. Prune it the day the README points at the rule by heading text instead of a line number.
